beats.title: Abu Bakr Becomes the First Caliph
beats.description: After the Prophet Muhammad's death, the community's leaders chose his companion Abu Bakr as its first successor.
beats.note: Muhammad's death and Abu Bakr's selection fall in the same year.

beats.title: Rashidun Victory at Yarmouk
beats.description: A caliph's army routed a larger Byzantine force by a river valley, opening Syria and Palestine to Muslim rule.

beats.title: Caliph Umar Takes Jerusalem
beats.description: The caliph accepted the surrender of the holy city's Christian patriarch and granted its people a covenant of safety.

beats.title: Battle of Nahavand Opens Persia
beats.description: A decisive victory over the Sasanian army, under Caliph Umar, left the Persian heartland open to conquest.

beats.title: Uthman Standardises the Quran
beats.description: The third caliph ordered one authoritative written text of the Quran and had copies sent to the main cities.
beats.note: Traditional date; no single authoritative year was found.

beats.title: Battle of the Camel
beats.description: The first civil war among Muslims began as Caliph Ali's forces defeated an army led by Aisha outside Basra.

beats.title: Muawiya Founds Umayyad Caliphate
beats.description: After Ali's death, the Syrian governor took the caliphate and made it a hereditary dynasty ruled from Damascus.

beats.title: Battle of Karbala
beats.description: The Prophet's grandson Husayn refused allegiance to a new caliph and fell with his band in Iraq, shaping Shia identity.

beats.title: Dome of the Rock Completed
beats.description: Caliph Abd al-Malik had a golden-domed shrine finished on the Temple Mount, the oldest surviving major Islamic monument.

beats.title: Great Mosque of Damascus Begun
beats.description: An Umayyad caliph started a vast mosque on the site of a Christian basilica in his capital.

beats.title: Umayyad Conquest of Spain
beats.description: A Berber-led army sent under the caliphate crossed the strait and defeated the Visigothic king, beginning Muslim al-Andalus.

beats.title: Umayyad Siege of Constantinople
beats.description: A large Umayyad army and fleet besieged the Byzantine capital for a year and failed, halting expansion in the west.

beats.title: Battle of Tours
beats.description: A Frankish army under Charles Martel turned back an Umayyad raiding force in central France.

beats.title: Abbasid Revolution
beats.description: A revolt from Khorasan overthrew the ruling dynasty of Damascus and installed a new line of caliphs.

beats.title: Battle of Talas
beats.description: An Abbasid army beat a Tang Chinese force in Central Asia, and papermaking later spread west from captives.

beats.title: Al-Mansur Founds Baghdad
beats.description: The Abbasid caliph laid out a circular capital on the Tigris that would become a great world city.

beats.title: Harun al-Rashid Becomes Caliph
beats.description: The ruler later remembered in the Arabian Nights took the Abbasid throne at the height of Baghdad's splendour.

beats.title: Elephant Gift Sent to Charlemagne
beats.description: Harun al-Rashid sent a white elephant named Abul-Abbas across the Mediterranean as a gift to the Frankish emperor.
beats.note: Annals record the journey in 801; arrival at Aachen is usually 802.

beats.title: Al-Ma'mun Wins Abbasid Civil War
beats.description: After a war with his brother over the succession, a scholarly caliph took control of Baghdad.

beats.title: Caliph Launches the Mihna
beats.description: A caliph forced scholars and judges to affirm that the Quran was created, punishing those who refused.

beats.title: Al-Mu'tasim Founds Samarra
beats.description: An Abbasid caliph moved his court and Turkish guards to a new palace city north of Baghdad.

beats.title: Fatimid Caliphate Proclaimed
beats.description: A rival Shia caliph was declared in North Africa, challenging both Baghdad and Cordoba for leadership of Islam.

beats.title: Cordoba Caliphate Proclaimed
beats.description: The emir of Cordoba took the title of caliph, creating a third rival caliphate in the Muslim world.

beats.title: Madinat al-Zahra Palace City Begun
beats.description: The Cordoban caliph began a royal palace city outside his capital to display the power of his new caliphate.

beats.title: Buyids Seize Baghdad
beats.description: A Persian dynasty entered the capital and reduced the Abbasid caliph to a figurehead under their control.

beats.title: Fatimids Take Egypt, Found Cairo
beats.description: A Fatimid army took Egypt and founded a new walled city that became the caliph's capital.

beats.title: Caliphate of Cordoba Abolished
beats.description: Andalusian notables formally ended the caliphate after years of civil war, splitting al-Andalus into small kingdoms.

beats.title: Seljuk Tughril Enters Baghdad
beats.description: A Turkic sultan entered the capital and was recognised by the Abbasid caliph, who became his religious figurehead.

beats.title: Basasiri Takes Baghdad for Fatimids
beats.description: A Turkish general seized Baghdad and had the rival Fatimid caliph proclaimed in the Abbasid capital, forcing the Abbasid caliph out.
beats.note: Seizure was at the end of 1058.

beats.title: Fatimid Succession Splits Ismailis
beats.description: When the Fatimid caliph died, a disputed succession divided his followers into rival branches that lasted for centuries.

beats.title: Almohads Claim the Caliphate
beats.description: A Berber reformist movement took Marrakesh, and its leader adopted the title of caliph in the Maghreb.

beats.title: Saladin Ends the Fatimid Caliphate
beats.description: Saladin had the sermon read in the name of the Abbasid caliph, ending Shia caliphal rule in Egypt.

beats.title: Al-Nasir Revives Abbasid Power
beats.description: A new Abbasid caliph began rebuilding the dynasty's authority in Iraq after generations under foreign soldiers.

beats.title: Mongols Sack Baghdad
beats.description: Hulagu's army took the Abbasid capital and executed the caliph, ending the caliphate in Iraq.
beats.why_in: end of the Abbasid caliphate in Baghdad

beats.title: Abbasid Caliphate Restored in Cairo
beats.description: The Mamluk sultan installed a surviving Abbasid relative as caliph, giving his rule religious legitimacy.

beats.title: Khilafat Movement Begins in India
beats.description: Indian Muslims launched a mass campaign to defend the Ottoman caliph's position after the First World War.

beats.title: Sultanate Abolished, Caliph Kept
beats.description: Turkey's assembly ended the sultanate but left a separate caliph with only a religious role.

beats.title: Turkey Abolishes the Caliphate
beats.description: The Turkish assembly deposed the last caliph and expelled his family, ending an institution that had lasted centuries.
